channel.title: Weekly Worker — Society & Culture (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker — Society & Culture.

item.title: Health under attack
item.description: What lies behind the surge of measles cases in the USA? It is not just Donald Trump and his health secretary. James Linney blames the general environment of disinformation and distrust in science
item.dc:creator: James Linney

item.title: Time has run out
item.description: Antalya ended in complete failure. But the big victory scored by the oil producers and fossil fuel lobbyists underlines that the whole Cop merry-go-round has done nothing to halt the rise in global temperatures. Michael Roberts provides the damning facts and figures
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Wholly Jewish in implementation?
item.description: It is not western Jewry that is to blame for the ongoing genocide in Gaza. To say otherwise is to mistake the symptoms for the disease, says Tony Greenstein in his open letter to Susan Abulhawa
item.dc:creator: Tony Greenstein

item.title: Socialism, gentrification and abjection
item.description: Paul Demarty reviews Fredrik deBoer All in your head Simon & Schuster 2026, pp291, £20
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Turn fear into active use
item.description: Calls for public ownership and democratic control are all well and good, but what about now? The left needs to embrace AI and employ it for our own purposes. As a first step, says Yassamine Mather, we need to know how the technology works. After that we can develop, master and apply
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Celebrity culture in the dock
item.description: With the conviction of Russell Brand on one count of rape and three of sexual assault, and now the David Walliams allegations, Paul Demarty calls for self-critical reflection on the left and a healthier, more egalitarian sexual culture
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Dancing the word
item.description: Jack Conrad reviews Chris Knight and Jerome Lewis The revolutionary origins of language New Haven CT 2026, pp384, hbk £25
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Slavery’s imperial apologists
item.description: Charles Windsor has not apologised for Britain’s role in Caribbean slavery. Nor has Andy Burnham. Mike Macnair says the official arguments against apologies and reparations are bogus. But to really right the wrongs of the past requires the overthrow of the world capitalist order
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Bertolt Brecht and Holy Joy
item.description: Culture can bring together theatre, poetry, music, stand-up comedy, anthropology and communist politics. That, explains Tam Dean Burn, is the ambition of the Diderot Gesellschaft Movement
item.dc:creator: Tam Dean Burn

item.title: Nature cannot go ignored
item.description: There are still those on the left who say ‘labour creates all wealth’. Seemingly militant, seemingly pro-worker, seemingly anti-capitalist, but profoundly wrong, says Jack Conrad
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: New age of security chaos
item.description: PHP2Shell is the latest of many disastrous security vulnerabilities. Their discovery and exploitation are easier than ever in the age of AI. Buckle up, advises Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty
